text: In the ray-optic model of a silicon (n = 3.48) core / silicon-dioxide (n = 1.44) cladding waveguide, total internal reflection guides light only when the ray's angle of incidence at the core-cladding interface (measured from the surface normal) exceeds the critical angle. What is this critical angle?
explanation: The critical angle is theta_c = arcsin(n2/n1) = arcsin(1.44/3.48) = 24.5 degrees. 44 degrees is the critical angle for a silica-to-air interface (arcsin(1/1.44)), a common mix-up; 65.5 degrees is the complement, i.e. the ray angle measured from the interface rather than the normal; 90 degrees would imply no guidance at all.
